subject: physics
title: Moments, levers and gears
key_idea: (Separate science) A force can turn an object about a pivot. The turning effect is the moment, **moment = force × perpendicular distance**. A balanced object has equal clockwise and anticlockwise moments. Levers and gears use this to transmit turning effects.

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers how a force makes an object rotate and how to calculate the turning effect.

items.meaning: The fixed point an object turns around.
The turning effect of a force about a pivot.
The two directions a force can turn an object about a pivot.

items: A force can cause an object to rotate about a pivot.
A bigger force gives a bigger moment.
A bigger distance from the pivot gives a bigger moment.
The distance is measured at right angles from the pivot to the line of action of the force.

blocks.label: Moment of a force
where: M is the moment of the force in newton-metres (N m).
F is the force in newtons (N).
d is the perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force in metres (m).

blocks.text: Convert centimetres to metres before substituting. Divide by 100.

items.text: A force of 2.0 N acts 7.5 cm from a pivot: 7.5 cm = 0.075 m.

diagram.alt: Calculate the moment of a force when the distance is given in centimetres.
diagram.question: A force of {F} N acts at right angles to a spanner, {d} cm from the pivot. Calculate the moment of the force in N m.

items: The moment of a force is its turning effect about a pivot.
M = F × d, with d measured at right angles from the pivot.
The unit is the newton-metre (N m).

sections.heading: Balanced objects and the principle of moments

blocks.text: (Separate science) This section covers what happens when the turning effects on an object are equal.

blocks.label: Principle of moments
blocks.formula: total clockwise moment = total anticlockwise moment
where: Both moments are taken about the same pivot.
This is true when the object is balanced, which means it is in equilibrium.

items: If the clockwise moment is bigger, the object turns clockwise.
If the anticlockwise moment is bigger, the object turns anticlockwise.
If the two moments are equal, the object does not turn.
To rebalance an object, change a force or move it to a different distance from the pivot.

items.text: A 650 N load is 0.75 m from the pivot: moment = 650 × 0.75 = 487.5 N m.
A 160 N effort must give the same moment: 160 × d = 487.5.
d = 487.5 ÷ 160 = 3.05 m, which is about 3 m.

diagram.alt: Balance a see-saw by changing the force and distances on each side of the pivot.

inputs.label: Distance of left force from pivot
Distance of right force from pivot

outputs.label: Anticlockwise moment of the left force
Force needed on the right to balance

items: Balanced means total clockwise moment equals total anticlockwise moment about the same pivot.
To balance with a smaller distance, you need a bigger force.

blocks.text: (Separate science) Levers and gears are simple machines that transmit the turning effect of a force.

items: A lever turns about a pivot, also called a fulcrum.
The effort is the force you apply. The load is the force you want to move.
If the effort is further from the pivot than the load, the moments can be equal with a smaller effort.
This makes the lever a force multiplier. A crowbar and a wheelbarrow work this way.
Meshed gears have teeth that fit together.
A force on one gear causes a moment about the pivot of the next gear, so it turns.
The second gear turns in the opposite direction.
The smaller gear, with fewer teeth, turns faster than the larger gear.
A small gear driving a large gear gives a bigger moment on the large gear, so the pair works as a force multiplier.

blocks.label: Meshed gears
blocks.formula: turns of gear A × teeth on gear A = turns of gear B × teeth on gear B
where: Turns is the number of complete turns of that gear.
Teeth is the number of teeth on that gear. The same number of teeth pass the meshing point on both gears.

items.text: A gear with 20 teeth turns a gear with 60 teeth, and the large gear makes 2 turns.

items: A lever with the effort far from the pivot needs less force to balance the load.
Meshed gears turn in opposite directions and the smaller gear turns faster.

checks.q: A force of 20 N acts at right angles 0.30 m from a pivot. Calculate the moment of the force.

checks.a: For a system in equilibrium, the sum of the clockwise moments equals the sum of the anticlockwise moments about the same point.

checks.q: Explain why the effort needed to lift the load with a wheelbarrow is smaller than the load.
checks.a: The effort is at a bigger distance from the pivot than the load, so a smaller force gives the same moment.

worked_example.question: A child applies a force of 2.0 N on gear A of a toy. The perpendicular distance between the force and the pivot is 7.5 cm. Calculate the moment of the force about the pivot.
worked_example.tip: One mark for converting the distance, one for substituting and one for the answer. A correct substitution of a distance that was not converted still earns the substitution mark.

worked_example.question: A lever is used to lift a heavy load. The weight of the load is 650 N. The centre of the load is 0.75 m from the pivot. An effort of 160 N is applied to the end of the lever to balance the load. Calculate the distance between the effort and the pivot.
answer_points: Moment of the load = 650 × 0.75 = 487.5 N m
distance = 487.5 ÷ 160 = 3.05 m, which rounds to 3 m (490 ÷ 160 gives 3.1 m)
worked_example.tip: Marks are for substitution, rearrangement and evaluation. Any value that rounds to 3 is accepted, and a power of ten error loses marks. Full marks for the correct answer without working.

worked_example.question: A boy of mass 70 kg stands on the end of a diving board at a distance of 1.8 m from the wall. Calculate the moment of the boy standing on the diving board. Gravitational field strength on Earth = 10 N/kg.
worked_example.tip: A correct answer of 1260 N m, or 1300 N m, scores all 4 marks. Using mass instead of weight loses a mark.
